experiences.title: The Sensory Date

prose_blocks.heading: In short
prose_blocks.text: Sequence sound, scent, texture, taste, and light, and add only the touch you have both marked welcome.

prose_blocks.heading: The hook
prose_blocks.text:
You can have a lovely dinner and still have skipped this chapter. A single candle on a restaurant table is atmosphere you happened to sit inside. The Sensory Date is built, before the room changes, from music, scent, texture, taste, light, and welcome touch. You use a few of those, in order, at an intensity you can both stand. You may retire a channel and stay on the date. You may skip touch and still be in the middle of it.

The other way to miss it is to turn every dial up at once. Bass, perfume, citrus, wool, dimness, and hands, all in the first minute, make a lobby with better intentions. Sequence is the courtesy.

prose_blocks.heading: Why it might matter
prose_blocks.text:
An evening becomes specific when you decide what a body is being asked to notice. One piece of music. One temperature of fruit. A sleeve in the hand. A lamp you can still see by. Choice gives either of you an exit before the room is already full of oil and noise.

Wanted affectionate touch has a research neighbor, and only for that channel. J2017 is a review and a model arguing that wanted affectionate touch can relate to relational, psychological, and physical well-being, including stress-related pathways. Unwanted touch sits outside that claim. The review does not test the rest of this date. See the notes.

The evening as a whole is a design, not a treatment. Sex is a separate decision, made outside the sequence. If you want it on the map at all, you say so in plain language before the first station, and either of you can take it back off the map.

If the wait before a planned evening is the thing you want to play with, build that in [The Art of Anticipation](035), and let this date be the landing only when the outline says so.

prose_blocks.heading: Before you begin
prose_blocks.text:
Choose the materials together, before anyone sets the scene. One person building a stage and inviting the other in at the end has prepared a different event.

Agree a budget, including a version that spends nothing and uses what is already home. Alcohol is not a material. Agree whether the evening stays nonsexual. The standing assumption is that it does, until both of you say otherwise before you start.

Gather only what you named.

- **Music.** A short playlist you have the right to play, volume agreed in advance. Instrumental, if lyrics, hearing, or tinnitus make words a problem. Silence can stand in for music when another channel is being used on purpose.
- **Scent.** Unscented is the default. Any scent is opt-in, low, and in a room you can air. Asthma, migraine, and allergy get the unscented room without a debate. A surprise oil breaks the agreement.
- **Texture.** One or two: a blanket, a sleeve, a warm cup. Bring them to the seat. The date is not a search through closets.
- **Taste.** A few bites that respect allergies, texture aversions, and diet. Water counts.
- **Light.** Lamps you can raise as well as lower. Ordinary bulbs and high contrast are welcome. Dimness is optional. Strobing and near-darkness are not the house default. If seeing the room matters for comfort or balance, keep it seeable.
- **Touch.** A plan that can be the word "none." If there is a plan, name forms in words: hands, a kiss on the hair, a palm between the shoulder blades, over clothes, for a few minutes. Only the overlap of what both of you marked will be on the table later.

"Stop" ends a station. "Less" is the useful smaller word when you need the volume down, the scent gone, the bite smaller, or the hand lighter. Practice saying both before the first station, once, so they exist as ordinary vocabulary.

If a sense is unavailable, sore, or simply unwelcome, substitute and continue.

- Sound can become captions, an instrumental, a line you read quietly to yourself, or a skipped station while you host taste or texture instead.
- Scent can become fresh air, a closed window, or a named decision to have no scent station.
- Taste can become a sip of water, a change in temperature, or the warm cup kept as texture when bites are off the table.
- Light can stay as the lamps already are. You can describe that choice in a sentence. You do not have to darken a room to make it count.
- Touch can be retired without retiring the date. Someone may put a blanket on their own body if they want pressure without a partner's hands. A partner's hands do not arrive as the substitute for a station that was declined.
- At a distance, a shared playlist and the same tea at the same time count as a reduced remote version. Call it reduced. It is not the touch station.

The date comes to the person who is seated or lying down. They do not tour the apartment to earn the evening.

prose_blocks.heading: The experience
prose_blocks.text:
The standard date takes about 45 to 75 minutes.

**Boundaries, about 10 minutes.** Read the touch plan. Read the agreement about sex, which is "off the map" unless you both put it on before this minute. Name any channel that is off for the night. "Maybe if the mood changes" is how a retired channel sneaks back in. Pick "off" or "on."

**Choose hosts.** Each of you picks one channel to host. Choose a third station together, or let the third be quiet background: a lamp already at the agreed level, a texture within reach, one piece of music under everything else. Channels you did not choose are that background, or they are explicitly off. Three stations, in sequence. Six sensations at full strength mean you have left the design.

A workable arc: light at a level both of you can stand, one piece of music, one taste, one texture within reach. Touch, when it is welcome, is its own station afterward. It is not a sauce poured over the others.

**Run the stations, about 10 to 15 minutes each.** Each hosted station stays behind a fresh offer from the host for that station. A yes to the date, or to the station you just finished, does not start the next one. If the third station is more than background, one of you offers it and waits for an answer. The host says what they chose and how to come down, in one or two sentences, and waits. "Orange slices, cold, four of them. Say less if you want them smaller. Say stop if you want them gone. Do you want this station?" The guest says yes, asks for a smaller version, or declines. A decline retires that station and leaves the date going. Then the guest notices, and uses those words. You may talk. You may be quiet. You do not score each other's bodies.

Host with a light hand.

- Music: one piece, or three short ones you named. Shuffle is a surprise. Skip it.
- Scent, only if opted in: a peel on a plate, a window, a single low note in the air. Not a diffuser you cannot shut off quickly.
- Texture: offer the choice. Linen or wool. Cup or blanket. The guest's hand decides.
- Taste: small, named, easy to refuse after one bite.
- Light: set it, then leave it. Ask once if it needs to come up.

**Touch, only if you both marked at least one form welcome.** Restate the overlap before anyone moves. That restatement is a fresh offer for this station. Wait for a yes to the form you are about to use. A yes to music, scent, texture, taste, or light does not cover it. Whoever is being touched sets the pressure and the placement, and may shrink the menu again in the moment. Either of you can be that person. Stop ends it. If either of you marked none, skip the station, drink the water, and remain on the date. A skipped touch station is a finished one.

**Close, about 5 minutes.** Name the channels you used, the ones you would repeat, and the touch decision: the forms that were welcome, or none. If desire showed up, you may say so as a fact about yourself. You do not owe it a sequel. If sex was never on the map, the close is not the moment it climbs on. If it was on the map, it still needs a present yes, after the stations, in a separate sentence. Momentum is not that sentence.

prose_blocks.heading: Three ways to play
prose_blocks.text:
**Short, 20 minutes.** One channel each. Agree the boundaries in a few sentences. Each hosted station waits for a fresh offer from its host. Run the two stations, and name what you would repeat. Background stays quiet. Touch waits, unless it was a channel someone chose and both of you had already marked that form welcome. Even then, the host offers that form and waits.

**Standard, about 60 minutes.** Boundaries, two hosted stations, each behind a fresh offer from its host, one background or third station, the touch station under the overlap rule, and the close.

**Extended, about 90 minutes.** After the first pass, take a second round. Repeat a channel only behind a fresh offer from the host. Retire one that was too much, and say why in a single sentence. The second round can be "Orange again?" and a yes, while the wool stays on the chair. That is a complete extended date.

prose_blocks.heading: Going deeper
prose_blocks.text:
If the first taste was welcome, offer one contrast. Salt after sweet, warm after cold, still inside diet and allergy. The contrast is its own offer. Wait for a yes. One contrast is enough.

Next time, swap hosts. The person who received the music chooses it. The person who plated the food gets to be offered a bite, and gets to refuse it.

During a station, one sentence of want is allowed. "I like your wrist in this light." It is attention. It does not book anything, and it does not expand the touch menu. "Thank you" is a complete reply.

Neighbors, on their own nights: [The Language of Touch](022) for a vocabulary of nonsexual touch, [The Sixty-Second Embrace](023) for one timed embrace, and [The Slow Dance With No Music](038) for a silent sway without stations.

prose_blocks.heading: Variations and replay
prose_blocks.text:
Zero budget, at home: water in a glass you like, a sleeve you already own, one lamp, one song you already have the right to play, touch none or hands only.

Outdoors, keep only the channels the place can hold. A shared piece of fruit and one song at an agreed volume can be the short version. Skip partner touch in public unless you both marked a public form in advance.

Pain and sensory aversion: retire the loud channel first. Low energy: the short version, materials already in the seat, host jobs of one sentence each.

Keep a private note of what you would repeat. Next time, start there. Add a retired channel back only if the person who retired it asks.

The reduced remote version stays labeled. Same playlist, same tea, cameras optional. Do not add a "touch the screen" substitute and call it the touch station. If you want the in-person date later, put it on a plan you both write. That plan can borrow its wait from 035.

prose_blocks.heading: Examples
prose_blocks.text:
Rowan and Vale are fictional. They are not the two of you.

Before the room changes, they agree: nonsexual, unscented because Rowan gets headaches from fragrance, budget zero, "stop" and "less" as the words. The reading lamp stays bright enough to see a plate. Music is one instrumental they both already own, quiet, background, not a hosted station. Scent is off, and they say "off" so the absence is a choice.

Rowan hosts taste and offers it before the plate moves. "Four cold orange slices. Less if you want them smaller. Say stop if you want them gone. Do you want this station?" Vale says yes. Vale hosts texture and offers before either cloth is handed over. "Linen sleeve or wool throw, in your hand. Less, or stop. Do you want this station?" Rowan says yes to linen. The wool stays on the chair, available and not applied.

Touch uses the overlap only, offered again before anyone moves: hand-holding, and a kiss on the shoulder, over clothes. Vale says yes to both. Rowan sets light pressure. After the shoulder kiss, Vale says stop. The wool on the chair was already a lot to have in view, and the kiss tipped it. Rowan stops, refills the water, and they finish the orange. Nobody treats the stop as a failed seduction.

In the close, Rowan wants the orange again. Vale wants the linen again and wants the wool retired. Touch decision: hands yes another time, shoulder kiss not tonight, and not a promise. They leave sex where they put it, which was off the map. The orange was the sensation worth keeping. That is a successful date.

prose_blocks.heading: Afterward
prose_blocks.text:
- Which channel had the right intensity, and which needs to be smaller or gone?
- Did a substitute work, or do you need a different one next time?
- Did "stop" or "less" get used, and did the date continue after it?
- What do you want repeated, with no score attached to a body?

You can answer in four short lines, or you can sit in the lamp you already agreed on and let the orange be the answer. Both closes count.

prose_blocks.heading: Our Story
prose_blocks.text:
Use this spread for the date you just made. Private pages are optional to share. Record channels, what you would repeat, and the touch decision. Leave body scores off the page.

```journal
session: date, time, place, version played, mood if wanted, intention, initials if wanted, done or paused
partner_a:
- The channel I hosted, and how I chose its intensity
- The touch I wanted, in what form, or none, and whether the overlap matched
partner_b:
- The channel I hosted, and a sense that needed a substitute or a lower setting
- What I would repeat, and what I would retire, without grading my partner's body
shared:
- What actually happened
- The line or moment worth keeping
- What we discovered
- What we might do next, if anything
revisit:
- Attempt, date, and what changed
- Then versus now
```

prose_blocks.heading: Notes
prose_blocks.text: See J2017. Jakubiak and Feeney review wanted affectionate touch and offer a model arguing that it can relate to relational, psychological, and physical well-being, including stress-related pathways. Unwanted touch is outside that claim. Their paper is not a trial of a multi-sensory date, and it does not test music, scent, texture, taste, or lighting. No citation is claimed for those channels. The evening is a reimagined design. Clinical sensate focus is a different procedure and is not reproduced here.

experiences.title: The Desire Nobody Asked About

prose_blocks.heading: In short
prose_blocks.text: Name a wish you have never asked for, and let it stay a wish.

prose_blocks.heading: The hook
prose_blocks.text:
Some wants get good at waiting. They are not the tea, the ordinary kiss, or the show you both like. They are the ones nobody asked about, so they never had to survive a pause. This chapter takes one of them out and leaves it on the table.

You discuss previously unexpressed wishes, fantasies, or forms of affection without obligations to act. The wish is allowed to remain a wish. One of you names something previously unasked. The other receives it. Curiosity is the activity, plus one sentence said out loud: hearing it is not a yes. If the evening ends by scheduling the wish, the chapter has been replaced by a negotiation.

prose_blocks.heading: Why it might matter
prose_blocks.text:
One wish, previously unasked, and a sentence said out loud: hearing it is not a yes. The wants that already fit the life you share are easy to schedule. This hour is for one that has been waiting. A clean hearing is a different event from a plan.

Diary studies of ordinary interactions found that intimacy tracked self-disclosure and partner disclosure, with perceived partner responsiveness as a partial mediator, and that in Study 2 emotional disclosure predicted intimacy more strongly than factual disclosure. See L1998 in the notes. Those diaries did not study fantasy, did not assign this conversation, and do not show that naming a desire changes a relationship. This chapter will not line your appetites up or repair a dry spell. It lets an unspoken want be heard without becoming a work order.

The Yes, No, Maybe Game sorts ideas and compares lists. This chapter handles what had not been asked, including wishes that will never be enacted. The Intimacy Blueprint maps conditions. Here you disclose one unasked wish. Confession Without Consequence is receptive listening. It is not immunity for harm, and it does not license you to ignore the mark on a desire.

prose_blocks.heading: Before you begin
prose_blocks.text:
Sit where you can write, or set a voice note, or agree to speak. Any of those completes a turn. Eye contact is unnecessary. Phones can stay in the other room unless one of them is the paper.

You each get three lanes, and you do not have to use them all.

1. An affectionate gesture nobody has requested. A greeting, a hand at the neck in public, an endearment, feet touching while you read.
2. A fantasy that may stay imaginary. Sexual, romantic, or mild.
3. A form of closeness you have edited out of ordinary talk. Pace, warmth, being desired while you are in pain or tired, a posture that does not hurt, silence or talk during sex, being left alone afterward.

Passing a lane is a complete turn. Say or write "pass." Sexual vocabulary is optional. Pain, fatigue, and limited mobility are full desires. If a wish needs someone who has not agreed, or if it depends on humiliation, mark it tell only and stop before any plan. This chapter will not supply a procedure for those acts. Long-distance works by voice or letter. Sensory overload means one wish and a planned pause. Either of you may pass the whole chapter.

Agree the listener's job before anyone shares. The listener restates what they heard, names something they appreciate about being told, and says, "Hearing this is not a yes." They do not solve, bargain, grade, or look to the speaker to take the wish back. The speaker then marks the item with one of three phrases: "tell only," "maybe another day," or "please do not ask me to do this."

prose_blocks.heading: The experience
prose_blocks.text:
The move is one unasked wish, written before it is spoken. Give the standard version 40 minutes. The short and extended cuts are below.

1. Apart, even if you are at the same table, write the wish before you speak. Two or three sentences are enough. Name the lane. A few minutes is the limit on the writing, if you want one. A voice note counts. If you are passing, the card says pass, and you can stop there.
2. One lane at a time. The speaker reads the note or plays it. They leave the wish at the size they wrote. If they hear themselves shrinking it ("it's stupid, never mind"), they may pause and either finish the original sentence or mark the turn passed. Both are clean. Apologizing a wish down to nothing is a habit this chapter interrupts.
3. The listener does three things, in order, and then stops.
   - Restate what you heard in plain language. Pause for a correction. "I heard that you want to be kissed slowly and told something specific about your mouth. Did I miss a piece?"
   - Name one thing you appreciate about being told. Appreciate the telling. A review of the wish is a different activity. "I appreciate that you let me hear the shy part without a joke glued to it" is the job. "We should do that on Thursday" is not.
   - Say the sentence. "Hearing this is not a yes." Say it even if you would have said yes in some other conversation. Especially then. Your enthusiasm is not a signature.
4. The speaker marks the item out loud. "Tell only." "Maybe another day." "Please do not ask me to do this." One mark. The listener does not haggle the mark up or down.
5. Switch. The second wish does not have to use the same lane, the same heat, or the same amount of courage. A small affectionate want is a full turn beside a sexual fantasy.
6. Silence is not assent. If the listener goes quiet, the speaker asks, "Do you want a moment, or are you done responding?" The listener picks one. A moment gets a minute. Done means they return to whichever of the three jobs they skipped, or they say "pause" and the turn waits. Quiet does not mean yes, no, or wounded. Those require words.

Three predictable misses have a repair.

If the listener starts solving, they stop and return to the restate. A pillow, a date, a toy, or a technique waits for another conversation, and only if the mark is "maybe another day" and the speaker brings it back. This chapter does not book the wish.

If the listener bargains ("I'll do yours if you do mine"), the turn ends. A wish is not a debt. Sit quietly, then continue with another lane or stop for the night.

If the listener looks hurt and the speaker rushes to retract, either person says "pause." The wish stays as told. The listener may say, "This landed in a sore place, and I can still do my three jobs," and then do them. Comfort after the mark is welcome. It is not a retraction.

prose_blocks.heading: Three ways to play
prose_blocks.text:
### Short, 20 minutes

One lane each. Use 3 minutes to agree the listener's three jobs, 5 minutes to write in parallel, and 5 minutes per person to tell, restate, appreciate, say the sentence, and mark. The last 2 minutes repeat the marks. Stop. A single lane is the whole activity.

### Standard, 40 minutes

Use 6 minutes on the rules and 8 minutes to write up to three lanes. Share one lane at a time, alternating, about 4 minutes a turn. Six turns plus a 2-minute close fill the 40 minutes. Fewer lanes end earlier, and that ending is correct. You may pass a lane. You still do not schedule anything.

### Extended, 70 minutes

Do the standard sitting. Then leave the table for 10 minutes. Tea, a window, laundry, anything that is not this conversation. After the pause, a "maybe another day" returns only if the person who owns it brings it back, and only inside the remaining 20 minutes. The listener uses the same three jobs. The second pass still does not set a date. If nobody brings a maybe back, say, "That was the telling," and end. Ending because a wish stayed a wish is a correct use of the longer sitting.

prose_blocks.heading: Going deeper
prose_blocks.text:
A tell-only mark protects imagination. Some fantasies arouse because they stay stories: being watched while you undress, being wanted in a particular room, a kind of power you do not want imported into Tuesday. Your partner can find the story beautiful and still have no standing to request it later.

A maybe means the speaker may open a different conversation on another day. The listener does not circle back as a surprise. "Please do not ask me to do this" is a closed door. Curiosity about why is something the speaker may offer. It is not owed.

If a wish barely includes you, or stings, do the three jobs before you discuss your own feeling. After the mark you can ask for water or a walk. Plenty of unasked desires are small, and the relief is that the small one was allowed to stay small. "I want warmth and no required position" is a complete desire. So is "I want you to talk dirtier than we ever have, and I want that sentence to be the end of it tonight."

prose_blocks.heading: Variations and replay
prose_blocks.text:
A voice note works. The reply contains the restate, the appreciation, and the sentence. A letter works the same way: those three pieces on the back, and no logistics paragraph.

On a later month, bring a new lane. A past maybe expires unless the speaker reopens it. A passed wish is not a score. If you want sex the same night for your own reasons, that is a new conversation with its own yes. It does not borrow consent from what you just heard.

prose_blocks.heading: Examples
prose_blocks.text:
Rowan and Vale are fictional. They are not the two of you.

They use the kitchen table and kill the overhead light. Rowan passes the affectionate-gesture lane and reads a fantasy. "I want to be kissed against the counter while the pan is still hot, and I want you to say what you like about my mouth. I have wanted that for a year. I am not asking you to do it." Vale puts both hands on a mug instead of becoming helpful. "I heard a kitchen kiss, the pan still going, and words about your mouth. About a year. You are not asking. I appreciate that you left it at its actual size. Hearing this is not a yes." Rowan marks it tell only. "If we turn it into a plan, I will start directing it. Directing is the part I keep editing out."

Vale's lane is a form of closeness. "When I am in pain I still want to be treated as someone you desire, not as a patient you are being good to. I don't have a position to request. I want the tone." Rowan almost offers a pillow arrangement for tonight, hears the solution forming, and stops. "I heard that pain doesn't cancel you as someone I might want, and that the tone matters more than a pose. This landed in a sore place, because I worry I have been careful in the wrong direction, and I can still do the three jobs. Thank you for trusting me with the part you usually translate into a joke. Hearing this is not a yes." Vale marks it maybe another day, and does not name the day.

Vale's last wish arrives tighter: being watched while undressing, slowly, with no commentary and no task. Vale marks it "please do not ask me to do this" before Rowan can fall in love with the image. Rowan restates it, thanks Vale for the boundary inside the telling, says the sentence, and does not ask why the door is closed. The closed door is the information. They put the notes in a drawer Rowan can empty alone.

prose_blocks.heading: Afterward
prose_blocks.text:
Repeat the marks if you want them said once more in a quieter voice. Thank each other for the three jobs, briefly. Then do something ordinary. Dishes, a show, sleep.

The paper is private unless the writer shares it. Shred it, or keep it somewhere the other person does not browse. A tell-only wish stays out of later flirtation. A maybe waits for the speaker. If it never returns, the hearing still counted.

prose_blocks.heading: Our Story
prose_blocks.text:
Use this spread for the sitting you just had. Private pages are optional to share. The person who wrote one decides. You can pass a prompt, change it, or leave it blank.

```journal
session: date, time, place, version played, mood if wanted, intention, initials if wanted, done or paused
partner_a:
- Which lane did you tell or pass, what was the wish in one sentence, and which mark did you give it?
- When you were the listener, what did you want to do with their wish, and what did you do instead?
partner_b:
- What was it like to hear a desire and leave it unanswered as a plan?
- Which wish of your own did you almost shrink, and what sentence did you manage to leave at full size?
shared:
- What actually happened
- The line or moment worth keeping
- What we discovered
- What we might do next, if anything
revisit:
- Attempt, date, and what changed
- Then versus now
```

prose_blocks.heading: Notes
prose_blocks.text:
The catalog premise is the mechanism: discuss previously unexpressed wishes, fantasies, or forms of affection without obligations to act. Yes / no / maybe sorts are practices, not a validated protocol, and this chapter does not reproduce a questionnaire.

See L1998. In diary studies of daily interactions, intimacy tracked self-disclosure and partner disclosure, with perceived partner responsiveness as a partial mediator. In Study 2, emotional disclosure predicted intimacy more strongly than factual disclosure. That finding is a neighbor. It is not a test of this chapter, not a study of fantasy, and not evidence that saying a desire aloud will change your relationship. No clinical trial of this activity is claimed.

experiences.title: The Slow Dance With No Music

prose_blocks.heading: In short
prose_blocks.text: Sway together in silence, with no steps to get right.

prose_blocks.heading: The hook
prose_blocks.text:
Put the music stand in the corner and leave it empty. The song is the part people hide inside: a chorus to tell you when to feel something, a beat to get right, an audience of relatives doing the same box step. This chapter keeps the sway and drops the rest.

Move together slowly in silence and explore unstructured closeness, with nobody required to lead the meaning. The dance does not have to become a conversation, a performance, or a sexual sequence. Words can come after. During the minutes you agreed, the minutes are the whole event.

prose_blocks.heading: Why it might matter
prose_blocks.text:
A lot of touch in a shared life is a doorway. Hello, goodbye, pass me that, squeeze past in the kitchen. A slow dance asks you to stay past the doorway, without a playlist supervising the mood.

A theoretical review argues that affectionate touch people actually want can relate to relational, psychological, and physical well-being, including pathways tied to stress. See J2017 in the notes. Unwanted contact sits outside that claim. The review is not a trial of silent dancing, and silence will not manufacture desire or reveal a couple's "real" chemistry. Tender, silly, or both at once can all happen inside the agreement you made about time and touch.

Slow dancing at a celebration is an ordinary custom. You are borrowing the sway, without a therapy protocol or a mindfulness course. The Silent Conversation sends meaning by gesture. The Sixty-Second Embrace is stillness on purpose. This is locomotion, however small, done together and without music. Eye contact belongs to Four Minutes of Forever. The Language of Touch is where you compare kinds of welcome contact. Here you choose a ceiling once, and then you move.

prose_blocks.heading: Before you begin
prose_blocks.text:
Agree the length before anyone touches anyone. About 3 minutes, or up to 8 minutes. Agree it in words, then put the words down.

Choose a form. These are equal dances, not a ladder from lesser to real.

- A standing sway. Matching height is unnecessary. A ballroom frame is unnecessary. Hands at a waist, a shoulder, or each other's elbows are all complete.
- A seated sway, knee to knee, with hands joined or resting where you both already agreed.
- Hand contact between a wheelchair user and a standing or seated partner. The chair can move a little, or the standing person's weight can shift. Shared movement can be that small.
- A shared rocking rhythm while lying down, if standing or sitting hurts, or if the floor or the bed is simply where you want to be.

Hands-only is a complete dance. Vision is unnecessary. If one of you is deaf, or if music is overwhelming, the silence is already the right version. Do not rescue the moment with a surprise speaker.

Name the touch ceiling in a sentence each. "Hands and shoulders, and I can shrink to hands." "Waist and upper back, no lower." The ceiling can drop mid-dance. It rises only if you stop, speak, and both agree. Agreeing to sway is not an agreement to sex. Arousal can show up as a sensation. It is not an instruction.

Pick a stop signal that works without a speech: two hand squeezes, or the word "pause" if a squeeze is unclear. Practice it once before you start. Stopping is part of the design. Vertigo and pain are reasons to use the chair or the floor. You do not push through freezing, pain, or a wish to stop.

Decide the lead. One of you offers direction for the first half, then you switch. Or nobody leads, and you follow the slower body.

Long-distance cannot share weight. A timed sway on video, each of you with your own chair, is an adaptation with a stated limit: you are moving at the same time, not together. Either of you may skip the dance entirely.

prose_blocks.heading: The experience
prose_blocks.text:
The standard version takes about 30 minutes: agreements, 8 minutes of dancing, then a short debrief. Phones go face down in another room. Shoes are optional. One person can see the timer so the other does not have to watch it.

1. Each of you says the form and the ceiling in one sentence. If they differ, use the smaller ceiling and the form that both bodies can stay in. Write nothing down unless memory is unreliable. A note on the counter is enough.
2. Name the stop signal and practice it. Two squeezes, then a full release of the hands, or the word "pause," then you actually step back a few inches. The practice is not a joke about the practice. It is the rehearsal of an exit.
3. Say who leads the first half, or say that nobody does. If you are switching, agree the halfway cue now: a single tap on the hand, already defined, means "your half." The tap is not an invitation to talk.
4. Start the timer. Be quiet. Move. Shift weight. Turn a wrist. Rock. Take one slow step and then another, or stay inside a single square foot and let the sway do the traveling. Small is the design, not a failure of nerve.
5. If a joke shows up to keep the contact from settling, let one breath of it escape if it already has, then return to the movement. Commentary will hold the closeness at arm's length for the whole 3 or 8 minutes.
6. If you start correcting the other person's posture, you have left the dance. Stop correcting.
7. At halfway, switch with the cue you agreed, or keep following the slower body. No announcement.
8. If the stop signal happens, you stop. The person who stopped is the only one who can ask to restart. "Let's just finish the timer" does not count as that ask. Ending is a finished dance.
9. When the timer ends, separate by about a hand's width before anyone speaks. Those last seconds are still the dance.

The debrief can use words because the dance is over. Three questions are enough. What did you notice in the movement? Where was the touch too much, too little, or about right? Did you want to joke, stare, or turn it sexual, and what did you do with that? You do not grade chemistry. If you would rather stay quiet, nod, get water, and leave the questions for the journal. The dance still counts.

prose_blocks.heading: Three ways to play
prose_blocks.text:
### Short, 15 minutes

Use 5 minutes to choose the form, the ceiling, and the stop signal, including one practice. Dance in silence for 3 minutes. Hands-only and a chair both count. Use 7 minutes for the debrief questions, or fewer. Sensory overload is a reason to choose this length and to reduce skin contact. A 3-minute dance is complete.

### Standard, 30 minutes

Use 8 minutes to agree, practice the stop, and decide the lead. Dance for 8 minutes, and switch at 4 minutes if you are switching. Use about 14 minutes to separate, drink something, and answer the three questions. Up to 8 minutes is the long end of the dance itself. The rest of the half hour is preparation and words after.

### Why there is no extended version

A longer sway turns the silence into an endurance test. This chapter is a dance of about 3 minutes or up to 8 minutes. A still hold on purpose is The Sixty-Second Embrace. Messages sent by gesture are The Silent Conversation. Staying up until somebody "breaks" is a different game.

prose_blocks.heading: Going deeper
prose_blocks.text:
Awkwardness will offer a hum, a movie reference, a comment about a school gym. Let it pass and stay in the weight shift. The contact often gets more honest around minute 2, which is when people flee. You do not have to feel romantic for that minute to count.

Arousal may show up and stay unemployed. Warmth, breath, a hand, a familiar smell: bodies respond. Notice the wanting and let the timer finish. Sex, if anyone wants it, is a new agreement made in words after you have stepped apart. If only one of you feels it, you may say so in the debrief. The other person does not owe you their body in reply.

The shorter person does not get dipped. The person in pain does not get coached into a prettier line. If a hip complains, shrink the movement or sit, and continue at the new size. Freezing is a stop even before the squeezes. Say "pause," or open your hands. Save "this is nice" for after you have separated. During the timer, the sway can speak for itself.

prose_blocks.heading: Variations and replay
prose_blocks.text:
On another day you may add one quiet song, agreed in advance, volume low, either person free to cut it. That replay is a variation. The main version still has an empty music stand. If the song makes one of you perform, go back to silence next time.

Hands-only in a kitchen for 3 minutes, while the pasta water heats, is a legal replay. So is the lying-down rock on a morning when standing is a bad idea. The video adaptation stays labeled: each of you sways with your own chair for the same 3 or 8 minutes, and you say aloud that you cannot share weight. If the call drops, the dance is over. A roommate walking through is a reason to pause. An audience turns the sway into a show.

prose_blocks.heading: Examples
prose_blocks.text:
Rowan and Vale are fictional. They are not the two of you.

They clear a rug. Vale wants a standing sway and a hand at the waist. Rowan wants hands and forearms only, because a waist hold tips Rowan forward into a kind of sex they have not agreed to. They take Rowan's ceiling. Stop signal: two squeezes. Nobody leads. The timer is 8 minutes, which they will later admit was ambitious.

At about 2 minutes Rowan gets dizzy. Two squeezes. They stop. Vale's mouth is already loading a joke about a school dance. Vale lets the joke die unsaid, because the contact has only just become actual. Rowan asks to restart seated, knees touching, hands the same. Vale agrees. The second half is smaller and, to both of them, more like a dance. Vale feels a flicker of arousal and does not steer Rowan's hand anywhere new. When the timer ends they separate by a hand's width. Vale says, "I wanted to fill the quiet, and I also got turned on, and I am not asking for anything else." Rowan says, "Heard. The forearms were right. The dizziness was the stop. I am not saying yes to anything further tonight." They eat the pasta. The dance is over, and it was a dance.

prose_blocks.heading: Afterward
prose_blocks.text:
Water, or whatever you drink. A normal conversation can start. If you want a kiss, ask for the kiss. If you want the evening to become sexual, ask for that in words, with the same freedom to hear no. The sway does not carry those requests inside it.

If the dance stopped early, you do not schedule a makeup performance as a debt. You can try again another day at a shorter time and a smaller ceiling. You can also decide you have done it and you know what you think.

prose_blocks.heading: Our Story
prose_blocks.text:
The journal can be spoken into a note later if writing feels wrong in the afterglow or the awkwardness. Private pages are optional to share. The person who wrote one decides. Pass a prompt, change it, or leave it blank.

```journal
session: date, time, place, version played, mood if wanted, intention, initials if wanted, done or paused
partner_a:
- Which form and touch ceiling did you choose, and where in your body did the sway actually live?
- What did you do when you wanted to joke, correct a posture, or escalate?
partner_b:
- How did the silence sit with you, and did the touch stay at the size you chose?
- What changed at the halfway mark, or when the stop signal was used?
shared:
- What actually happened
- The line or moment worth keeping
- What we discovered
- What we might do next, if anything
revisit:
- Attempt, date, and what changed
- Then versus now
```

prose_blocks.heading: Notes
prose_blocks.text:
The catalog premise is the mechanism: move together slowly in silence and explore unstructured closeness. Slow dancing at a celebration is a social custom, not evidence. This chapter is not a dance-therapy protocol.

See J2017. Jakubiak and Feeney's review offers a theoretical model linking wanted affectionate touch in adulthood to relational, psychological, and physical well-being, including stress-related pathways. It is not a trial of silent dancing. Unwanted contact is outside the claim. No empirical citation is claimed for this dance as an intervention.

experiences.title: The Romantic Time Machine

prose_blocks.heading: In short
prose_blocks.text: Change the meeting, then name the attraction that is still this person.

prose_blocks.heading: The hook
prose_blocks.text:
End on the quality that survives the costume. Move the two of you: a different century, a delayed train, a job neither of you has, a city you have only passed through. Keep your actual faces. The costume can be ridiculous. The question underneath is strict.

Imagine one meeting in a different era or circumstance. Once the hat, the trade, and the accident of timing come off, what is still this person, and would it still draw you? If the scene never arrives at that question, you have been to a costume party. Charming, and not this chapter. 046, The Alternate Universe Couple, ends on one trait carried back from a shared plot. This chapter does not found a caper.

prose_blocks.heading: Why it might matter
prose_blocks.text:
The story of how you met is sticky. The bar, the app, the friend, the year the city felt a certain way. Attraction gets braided into that lighting until the person and the set are hard to separate. A changed meeting lifts the set. What remains is recognition, or a blank, and a blank is allowed.

"What if we had met another way" is a familiar romantic game. Treat it as imaginative play with a precise last question. It is not a clinical assessment, a past-life exercise, or a history exam. Nothing on this project's shelf shows that a counterfactual conversation increases desire or reveals a trait called chemistry, fate, or soulmates. The present relationship is not on trial. If the ferry is more charming than Tuesday, Tuesday is still the life you have. The chapter fails when the fantasy is used to call the real person a disappointment.

The Alternate Universe Couple invents other versions of you and follows their misadventures as a story. Keep that door shut. This chapter keeps the real persons and asks what would survive one changed meeting. The Moment I Knew, The Attraction Interview, and The Life Not Taken belong to other nights.

prose_blocks.heading: Before you begin
prose_blocks.text:
Each person chooses one meeting condition. An era is allowed. So is a circumstance with no costume: a delayed train, a different trade, a festival, a city neither of you has lived in, a night shift, a flooded bookstore, a ferry, a language class, an animal shelter after hours. You do not need a bibliography. If someone starts scoring historical accuracy, they are at the wrong party.

Either of you may discard a door. Keep circumstance prompts beside eras so nobody has to role-play a time that carries family pain, political pain, or bodily pain. If a scene only works by making one of you smaller under the law, pick another door. An era of legal inequality was not a simpler or more passionate world. The question is which quality belongs to the person in the room.

The imagined meeting is not a request to act a sex scene or to adopt period gender roles. Flirtation inside the fiction can be specific and adult. When the scene ends, nobody owes the kiss or the undressing to the actual evening. Skip the stock picture of a woman and a man in formal clothes. A research ship, a print shop, a night market, or two people covered in flour will do.

Talk or write. Long-distance fits. There is no mobility demand. Fatigue means one condition each and shorter sentences, which is already the shape. Either of you may pass and suggest a walk.

prose_blocks.heading: The experience
prose_blocks.text:
Use the standard version when you have about 40 minutes. The short version is the same skeleton without the private writing.

1. Apart, choose the condition. In the standard sitting, take about 8 minutes and write five lines: where, when, what each of you is doing, one sensory detail, and the moment you notice the other person. You are both yourselves. Clothes may change. Personalities may not.
2. Tell the scene in three beats, in this order, so the costume cannot eat the evening.
   - How you notice each other. A competence, a tenderness, a shameless interest in the food, or a body. "I would still want your hands" is a legal sentence.
   - Which quality is still this person, in language you could use on a Tuesday. "You still interrupt yourself when you get excited." "You still notice who has not been offered food." If the quality is stuck to the hat, take the hat off and try again.
   - One thing that other life would have hidden, which you are glad you know now. Illness, a friendship, a sexual truth, a grief, the silence after work. This beat keeps the game from becoming nostalgia for a life that never paid a bill.
3. If beat three becomes a complaint that real life is the dull version, return to beat two. The other meeting can be gorgeous, and you can still be glad you know the person who forgets lunch.
4. The listener has two sentences and no critique. "The quality I heard was ______. One quality I would still notice, even in that meeting, is ______." Add a recognition. Do not correct their history.
5. Switch. The second scene does not have to rhyme with the first. Comedy is welcome. Meanness is not.
6. Close with one line each. "What would still attract me is ______." If you cannot fill it, say so. An honest blank is a result. You do not repair it before you leave.

See each other, then get out. A plot, a villain, or a second decade is how people avoid the question. Love a detail, and still refuse to live in the costume for the whole sitting.

prose_blocks.heading: Three ways to play
prose_blocks.text:
### Short, 20 minutes

No writing. Take 3 minutes, total, to choose one condition each and discard any door that hurts. Give the first person 6 minutes for the three beats and the listener 2 minutes. Reverse that 8-minute block. Leave 1 minute for the closing lines. Short sentences still count. Use this for fatigue, a late night, or a bad connection.

### Standard, 40 minutes

Use 4 minutes to agree that the real persons stay, and that the present relationship is not being graded. Write in private for 8 minutes. Give each scene about 10 minutes, including the listener's two sentences. Leave 8 minutes for the closing lines and a little quiet, in case someone wants to scrap a scene and use the train instead. A discard is in time if it happens before you have spent the whole 10 minutes defending the first idea.

### Why there is no extended version

A second era, a plot, and invented selves belong to The Alternate Universe Couple. Stretching the costume until the surviving-attractor question never arrives is the failure this design prevents. One meeting each is the chapter. If you are tired, shorten the sentences. Do not add doors.

prose_blocks.heading: Going deeper
prose_blocks.text:
Name the kind of attraction. Sexual, aesthetic, intellectual, moral, comic, or two of those on one ferry. "I would still want your mouth when you are concentrating" and "I would still trust you with a frightened stranger" can share a scene. A vague "you have a vibe" fails because a Tuesday cannot recognize it.

The hidden thing you are glad to know is where you choose a person rather than a poster. The other life might have kept the charm and hidden the illness, the debt, the kink, the temper, the faith, the way grief sits in the house. Gladness does not mean the hard thing is easy. It means attraction is allowed to include reality. If you are not glad, skip the performance of gladness. Say what was hidden, and say you are still learning what to do with knowing it.

Listener, add a quality you have actually seen. "I would still notice that you track the exits and the feelings at the same time" is anchored. A timeless soul is fog. If the scene stirs a real wish, let it stand as a wish. On another day you can take it to The Desire Nobody Asked About, where hearing it will not be a yes. You can also let it evaporate. The time machine does not issue tickets.

prose_blocks.heading: Variations and replay
prose_blocks.text:
Write the five lines as a short letter and read them on a call. The listener still gets two sentences before you switch.

Make circumstance cards: train, night shift, bookstore flood, election-night kitchen, ferry, hospital cafeteria as visitors, animal shelter, language class, fair, research ship. Draw one. If either of you hates it, discard and draw again.

Replay with a new door. If you want the same ferry again because it was fun, say you are repeating it for pleasure, and still ask the three beats. A do-over until the attraction sounds impressive is a different game.

prose_blocks.heading: Examples
prose_blocks.text:
Rowan and Vale are fictional. They are not the two of you.

Rowan starts in a 1920s newsroom and scraps it almost at once. The scene wants Vale rescued, plus a quip about the hat, plus praise for a "simpler" era. New door: a night ferry between two cities neither of them has lived in, both of them covering someone else's shift. Rowan notices Vale giving the good blanket to a stranger and then looking embarrassed. The surviving quality is that Vale still hides a tenderness and gets shy about it. The ferry would have hidden Vale's ordinary silence after work, and Rowan is glad to know it, because that silence is how Vale comes back into a room. Vale answers, "The quality I heard was the hidden kindness. One quality I would still notice is that you track the exits and the feelings at the same time."

Vale's scene is an agricultural fair. Both of them are publicly bad at a pie. The noticing is sexual and comic at once: flour on Rowan's wrist, and the way Rowan loses without getting cruel. The surviving quality is competence failing in public while the person stays decent. The thing a pie contest would have hidden is Rowan's specific way of wanting, which Vale names in one plain sentence and does not ask to act out. Rowan reflects the decency, then adds a quality: "I would still notice that you narrate your own embarrassment before anyone else can use it."

They close. Rowan: "What would still attract me is the kindness you try to smuggle." Vale: "What would still attract me is the way you want, which I only know because this is the life we have." They do not grade the apartment against the ferry. They do the dishes that are actually in the sink.

prose_blocks.heading: Afterward
prose_blocks.text:
You can kiss if you both want a kiss. You can also make tea. The scene is not a request, and the more cinematic meeting does not get a vote on your evening.

If one of you feels a pang that real life is less scored with string quartets, say the pang in one sentence and then name the Tuesday quality again. The pang is human. Letting it steer the rest of the night turns the game into a complaint. You are allowed to prefer your actual person and still enjoy a ferry.

prose_blocks.heading: Our Story
prose_blocks.text:
Write while the scene is still warm, or the next morning. Private pages are optional to share. The person who wrote one decides. Pass a prompt, change it, or leave it blank.

```journal
session: date, time, place, version played, mood if wanted, intention, initials if wanted, done or paused
partner_a:
- What meeting did you choose, and what quality of this person survived the costume?
- What would that other life have hidden, and are you glad you know it?
partner_b:
- When you were listening, what quality did you reflect, and what quality did you add because you would still notice it?
- Which door did you discard, and what did the scene you kept let you say about attraction?
shared:
- What actually happened
- The line or moment worth keeping
- What we discovered
- What we might do next, if anything
revisit:
- Attempt, date, and what changed
- Then versus now
```

prose_blocks.heading: Notes
prose_blocks.text: The catalog premise is the mechanism: imagine meeting in a different era or circumstance and what would still attract you. No empirical citation is claimed. Counterfactual conversation has not been shown, in any source on the project whitelist, to increase desire or to reveal a stable trait called chemistry. No whitelist ID is cited for this chapter. The activity is imaginative play, not a study and not a past-life practice.

experiences.title: The Intimacy Blueprint

prose_blocks.heading: In short
prose_blocks.text: Draw what welcomes desire for each of you, then design one occasion as a hypothesis.

prose_blocks.heading: The hook
prose_blocks.text:
Desire has weather. Time of day, a closed door, a joke in the first 5 minutes, a hip that hurts, a sink of disputed dishes, a light that is too bright, a body that has not slept. You usually discuss it once the weather has already turned, which is a bad time for cartography.

Map the conditions that support romance and desire, what impedes them, and how to design for both partners. Both partners means two authors. A map with one handwriting is a preference list. When you are done, you will have designed one occasion that respects both maps. Call it a hypothesis. Designing it does not summon desire, and it does not book a sexual result.

prose_blocks.heading: Why it might matter
prose_blocks.text:
People already talk about mood, timing, privacy, and what kills the mood. The blueprint gives that talk a shape before anyone is disappointed: two columns each, a joint map with three kinds of marks, and one next occasion. An impediment is a condition. Exhaustion, alcohol, and pain are design facts, not character reports.

If you were about to sort the columns into five love languages and crown a primary one, set the quiz down. A review found little support for one primary love language, for the idea that there are exactly five, and for matching as what predicts satisfaction. People do seem to benefit from a range of affectionate behavior. See I2024 in the notes. That review does not validate this map. It only keeps the map from shrinking into a type.

What Loving Me Actually Looks Like compares gestures that feel like love. The Yes, No, Maybe Game sorts ideas into yes, no, and maybe. The Desire Nobody Asked About lets one unasked wish stay a wish. The Sensory Date builds an evening from sensory materials. This chapter is the prior map of conditions and impediments. No study is claimed for the blueprint. You are designing a room, a time, and a way of starting. You are not diagnosing desire, and you are not treating it.

prose_blocks.heading: Before you begin
prose_blocks.text:
Work separately first. Paper, index cards, large type, or a spoken list the other person writes only with permission. Two columns: conditions that support romance or desire for you, and conditions that shut them down.

Use what applies: time of day, privacy, humor, who initiates, rest, pain, alcohol, unfinished logistics, audience, lighting, noise, medication, caregiving, shift work, disability, delay on a call, whether a camera is on. Those are map entries, including the unglamorous ones.

You may leave any condition unnamed. Say "unnamed" aloud if you want the blank to stay blank. The other person does not pry.

A list that is only the other person's faults will wreck the hour. Rewrite an indictment as a condition before you bring it back. "I shut down when the dishes are still in dispute" can stay. "You never help" goes back to the pencil. "Two drinks make me far away" is a design fact, and so is fatigue.

Writing a condition is not a yes to sex on the night you design. Either of you may cancel. Canceling creates no debt and requires no replacement performance. Initiation has no gender. "I want to be asked," "I want to start," and "I want a window where either of us might move first, and no is a complete answer" are all usable. If welcome touch is one condition among others, keep it specific. Wanted affectionate touch has a research review behind it, and unwanted touch is outside that claim. See J2017. Your map may leave touch off entirely.

prose_blocks.heading: The experience
prose_blocks.text:
The standard sitting is about 50 minutes. Phones start in another room, unless a shared note is the paper.

1. Alone, fill both columns: what supports romance or desire, and what shuts them down. The limit on the draft is 12 minutes. Be concrete enough that a stranger could set the room. "Late evening, after I have eaten, door closed, a joke before any speech." "Overhead light, pain I will not perform through, being asked to decide every step." Five lines a column are plenty. Two is enough. Skip the polish.
2. Read your own list. Skip any unnamed line. The listener copies the line onto the joint map and does not cross-examine it. "Did you say afternoon?" is a fair question. "Why can't you relax?" is a different genre. Drop it.
3. Mark the joint map three ways.
   - Shared: you both named something compatible, such as privacy or food first.
   - Mine only: it matters on one map, and the other person can honor it without pretending it is their appetite.
   - Yours only: the same dignity in the other direction.
   Leave clashes visible. Bright humor and quiet can both stay. Morning and late night can both stay. This chapter designs one occasion, not a constitution. The other window can be another day. Averaging two bodies into one sad compromise erases the map.
4. Write the occasion. Include at least one supporting condition for each person, and remove one impediment. Read it as a hypothesis. "Thursday after food, logistics list closed, lights low, either of us free to initiate or decline. We will know afterward whether that was true." Add the cancel line: "Either of us can call this off without owing a different night."
5. The occasion can be romantic, sensual, sexual, or a quiet hour. Sex is not the proof the map worked. Record what the conditions did, including nothing. "Nothing stirred" is a finding, not a verdict and not a cue for a corrective performance.

prose_blocks.heading: Three ways to play
prose_blocks.text:
### Short, 25 minutes

Use 3 minutes on the rules, especially the cancel line and the ban on indictments. Take 8 minutes apart for two supports and two impediments each. Use 8 minutes to mark those lines shared, mine only, or yours only. Use 6 minutes for one small hypothesis. "Saturday morning, no agenda, the group chat in a drawer" can be the whole design. A short map is complete.

### Standard, 50 minutes

Use 5 minutes on rules and materials, 12 minutes on the private columns, 8 minutes to read them, 12 minutes on the three-mark map, and 13 minutes on the hypothesis, the cancel line, and one sentence about what counts as a finding. "If we are irritable, we stop and eat, and we do not call that a failed romance."

### Why there is no extended version

A longer sitting starts to look like a contract, then like a test of whether desire appears on cue. The map is done when one occasion respects both authors. Sensory materials belong to The Sensory Date, and still need a fresh yes. One unasked wish belongs to The Desire Nobody Asked About. Gestures that feel like love belong to What Loving Me Actually Looks Like. Extra time here makes the hypothesis heavier, not truer.

prose_blocks.heading: Going deeper
prose_blocks.text:
"Who starts" is a design variable. One of you may want pursuit and an easy no. The other may want a standing invitation they can decline without a speech. Write both. Inside the window you named, whoever is moved can move first, and "not this time" needs no story. If neither of you moves, the hypothesis still ran.

Pain, medication, and disability belong in the ink: posture, duration, a seat instead of a bed, a nap first, a position that stays optional. Lighting and sound are variables too. Dim, steady, no music, the fan left on because silence rings. That is the version that fits.

Long-distance maps name latency, cameras, and what privacy means in two rooms. "Camera off, both doors closed" is a real plan. So is "camera on the face, and either of us can end the call without a replacement scene." A shared mark is not more virtuous than mine only. A condition only one person needs still belongs on the map.

prose_blocks.heading: Variations and replay
prose_blocks.text:
Use three piles of cards: shared, mine only, yours only. On a call, name the pile. If combining clothed romance and sexual desire makes one of you go vague, draw those maps on different days. Say which map you are drawing. Both use the same marks and the same cancel line.

Replay when the season, the shift, the medication, or the last hypothesis changes. Old hypotheses expire. They do not become law. If you try the occasion, add one journal line for what the conditions did. Revise the card later. Leave each other's bodies as they are.

prose_blocks.heading: Examples
prose_blocks.text:
Rowan and Vale are fictional. They are not the two of you.

Rowan's supports: late evening, a closed door, food already eaten, a joke rather than a speech. Impediments: hip pain, a bright overhead light, an unfinished money argument, alcohol past one glass because it makes Rowan sleepy and then guilty. Vale's supports: afternoon, little or no music, the dog walked, the morning not already waiting, permission both to start and to stop. Impediments: being rushed, a camera, the group chat as an audience, having to set the mood every time.

They mark privacy and a closed logistics loop as shared. Low light, food first, and hip pain as a reason to stay seated or lying down are Rowan's alone, and Vale does not pretend to share the hip in order to be a good partner. Afternoon, and initiation that can come from either of them, are Vale's alone. Rowan would still prefer late evening. They leave that clash on the map.

The hypothesis: Sunday after lunch, phones in a drawer, lights low, a joke first, the option to stay clothed and seated, either person may start or cancel. They do not write "and then we have sex." The cancel line is on the card. When they try a version of it, Rowan's pain is louder than expected. They stop. Vale does not ask for a replacement performance. Rowan does not apologize for the weather. In the journal they write that low light and the joke worked, the hour of day was Vale's condition and it was honored, and pain removed the rest. The map did what a hypothesis is for. It was testable, and it was allowed to be wrong without turning either of them into the problem.

prose_blocks.heading: Afterward
prose_blocks.text:
Read the hypothesis once more. Hang it where you will both see it, or fold it into the journal. A private condition stays on that person's page. The shared card carries only what you both agreed to know.

Before the occasion, one sentence is enough. "Still good," or "Canceling, no replacement owed." During it, the ceilings you wrote still apply, and a new no still works. Afterward, record the finding in ordinary language. Desire showed up, or it did not. The joke helped. The hour was wrong. The dog was not walked and you pretended otherwise, which was informative. Then leave the blueprint alone until you mean to redraw it.

prose_blocks.heading: Our Story
prose_blocks.text:
The columns can live on these pages, or on the cards you keep. Private pages are optional to share. The person who wrote one decides. Pass a prompt, change it, or leave it blank. A condition you left unnamed stays unnamed here too.

```journal
session: date, time, place, version played, mood if wanted, intention, initials if wanted, done or paused
partner_a:
- Which conditions support romance or desire for you, and which conditions shut them down?
- What did you refuse to average away when you built the joint map?
partner_b:
- Which of your conditions is easy to honor, and which one asks for a real change in the room?
- What did you put in the hypothesis, and what will you treat as a finding rather than a verdict?
shared:
- What actually happened
- The line or moment worth keeping
- What we discovered
- What we might do next, if anything
revisit:
- Attempt, date, and what changed
- Then versus now
```

prose_blocks.heading: Notes
prose_blocks.text:
The catalog premise is the mechanism: map conditions that support romance and desire, what impedes them, and how to design for both partners. Ordinary talk about mood and timing is the folk neighbor. This blueprint is not a sex-therapy protocol, a medical assessment of desire, or a five-language system. No empirical citation is claimed for the mapping itself.

See I2024. Impett, Park, and Muise's review finds little support for one primary love language, for exactly five languages, and for matching as what predicts satisfaction. People do seem to benefit from a range of affectionate behavior. The citation keeps this chapter from becoming that quiz. It does not validate the blueprint.

See J2017. The review of wanted affectionate touch applies only if touch is one condition among others. Unwanted touch is outside that claim. The review is not a trial of this map.
